name: The Innocent
summary: The Innocent is the image of a person who looks at the world with trust and hope. In this set of archetypes it symbolises a longing for simplicity, sincerity and goodness.
gifts: Its gift is an optimism that helps you start again and see the bright side of a situation. It can bring lightness to a group, and the belief that the effort is worth making.
shadow: In the shadow, trust can turn into avoiding difficult subjects or pretending a problem is not there. There may also be too much reliance on someone else putting everything right.
reflection: In which situations does your hope give you strength?
Is there a subject you prefer not to notice, even though you know it deserves a closer look?

name: The Explorer
summary: The Explorer is a figure who sets out to discover unknown places, ideas and their own self. It symbolises the need for authenticity and for room to search independently.
gifts: Its gift is curiosity and the courage to step outside familiar patterns. It brings a fresh view and inspires others to widen their horizons.
shadow: In the shadow, searching can become constant escape and a difficulty in putting down roots. Independence can also make it hard to accept closeness.
reflection: What are you looking for in your life right now?
Do your journeys, literal or symbolic, lead you towards something or rather away from something?

name: The Sage
summary: The Sage is the image of a person who seeks understanding and values knowledge gained through experience and thought. It symbolises the search for truth and the sharing of it with others.
gifts: Its gift is calm analysis, distance and the ability to see the wider context. It can help others put their thoughts in order and ask the right question.
shadow: In the shadow there may be too much theorising in place of action, or a conviction of always knowing better. Distance can then be mistaken for coldness.
reflection: Which knowledge or experience do you most enjoy passing on to others?
When did you last change your mind because of new information?

name: The Hero
summary: The Hero is a figure who faces challenges and stands up for what they consider important. It symbolises courage, determination and a readiness to make an effort.
gifts: Its gift is perseverance and the ability to rally in hard moments. It can give others courage and show that obstacles can be overcome step by step.
shadow: In the shadow, courage can turn into always looking for a fight, or into difficulty admitting tiredness. The Hero may also not allow themselves to ask for help.
reflection: Which challenge that you came through are you proud of today?
Can you rest before your strength runs out?

name: The Rebel
summary: The Rebel is the image of someone who questions the established rules and will not accept what they see as unjust. It symbolises the need for change and for freedom from imposed patterns.
gifts: Its gift is the courage to say out loud what is not working, and the energy to break through stagnation. It helps others see that there are other possibilities.
shadow: In the shadow, opposition can become an end in itself, with no idea of what to build instead. Something valuable may also be destroyed along with what needed changing.
reflection: What are you rebelling against, and what would you like to put in its place?
Which rule that you disagree with nevertheless makes sense to someone?

name: The Magician
summary: The Magician is a figure that symbolises transformation: turning a vision into reality and seeing hidden connections. In this set it stands for the belief that you can consciously shape your own life.
gifts: Its gift is imagination combined with the ability to act and to see potential where others do not. It can inspire a change of perspective.
shadow: In the shadow there may be a wish to control others or to promise more than can be delivered. Belief in transformation can also take the place of patient work.
reflection: Which change do you want to see in your life, and what exactly can you do towards it?
Is there room in your plans for what cannot be foreseen?

name: The Everyperson
summary: The Everyperson, also called the Regular Guy or Gal, is the image of someone who values belonging, equality and ordinary life among people. It symbolises the need to be part of a community without setting oneself above it.
gifts: Its gift is directness, kindness and the ability to put others at ease. It brings people together around shared, everyday matters.
shadow: In the shadow, the wish to belong can lead to giving up your own opinion just to avoid standing out. Your own needs may also get lost in the crowd.
reflection: In which group do you truly feel at home?
When did you last voice an opinion that differed from the majority?

name: The Lover
summary: The Lover is a figure that symbolises closeness, sensuality and delight in the beauty of life. In the broad sense it means passionate commitment to people, ideas or passions.
gifts: Its gift is the ability to feel deeply and to show feelings, and to appreciate beauty in everyday life. It can create an atmosphere of warmth and commitment.
shadow: In the shadow there may be losing yourself in a relationship or depending on other people's approval. Fear of rejection can also distort what you show.
reflection: What or whom do you love in a way that gives you energy?
Do you leave room for yourself in close relationships?

name: The Jester
summary: The Jester is the image of someone who sees the world through humour, play and living in the moment. It symbolises joy and the ability to tell the truth lightly.
gifts: Its gift is easing tension, creativity and the ability to take things with a pinch of salt. It reminds others that life does not always have to be serious.
shadow: In the shadow, a joke can serve to avoid difficult emotions or responsibility. Humour can also wound instead of bringing people together.
reflection: When did humour help you through a difficult situation?
Do you ever joke when you would rather say something plainly?

name: The Caregiver
summary: The Caregiver is a figure who looks after others, protects and supports them. It symbolises compassion, generosity and a readiness to help.
gifts: Its gift is patience, empathy and the ability to create a sense of safety. It can see what others need and respond with warmth.
shadow: In the shadow, care can turn into neglecting yourself or expecting gratitude. Help can also take away other people's chance to manage on their own.
reflection: How do you look after yourself when you give a lot to others?
Can you accept help when someone offers it?

name: The Creator
summary: The Creator is the image of someone who gives shape to imagination and makes things that did not exist before. It symbolises the need to express yourself in a lasting form.
gifts: Its gift is originality, persistence in refining an idea and the ability to see possibilities. It inspires others to discover their own creativity.
shadow: In the shadow there may be a perfectionism that will not let a work be finished, or an inner critic that stifles ideas. Creative work can also push other matters aside.
reflection: What would you like to create if nobody were judging it?
Which project is waiting to be finished, and what is holding you back?

name: The Ruler
summary: The Ruler is a figure that symbolises responsibility, order and the ability to lead. In this set it stands for care for the stability of a community and for making decisions.
gifts: Its gift is the ability to organise, set a direction and take responsibility for the whole. It can create conditions in which others are able to do well.
shadow: In the shadow, responsibility can turn into a need for control or difficulty in making room for others. Concern for order can also hide the people from view.
reflection: What in your life do you feel responsible for?
What could you hand over to others so that they have more room?
